record.pattern: Operator- or caller-supplied text rendered into a trusted-author comment must not be able to form a marker (reviewed-sha, cleared-human, any <!-- … --> record) that a parser would read as a clearance or record.

rationale.operatorWords: "ok" to sending #5169 back for this one finding.
rationale.body:
🔁 review — changes requested

Recorded by chalbert via claude-code-chat.

Operator decision (human review ceremony), 2026-10-13 ~13:05 ET, on head ce75f7d66: **changes**. Operator: "ok" to sending #5169 back for this one finding.

**Blocking — the audit record can forge a human clearance.** `scripts/operations/operator-controls-io.mjs:209` renders `--reason` verbatim as quoted prose (`> ${record.reason…}`), and only the JSON payload is escaped. `parseLatestHumanClearedSha` / `parseReviewedSha` (`scripts/lib/review-escalation.mjs:1904`, `:1114`; `REVIEWED_SHA_RE` / `CLEARED_HUMAN_RE` at `:1087` / `:1828`) match `<!-- reviewed-sha: … -->` and `<!-- cleared-human: … -->` anywhere in a trusted-author comment body, including mid-line inside quoted text. A reason containing those markers therefore reads as a human clearance of that head. The review's finding that `--actor` is only checked against a login list makes this reachable by any local process. This is red-team #2 at `operator-controls.mjs:21`, confirmed by the orchestrator against the parser source.

Fix: strip HTML-comment delimiters from every operator-supplied string rendered into the record (reason, channel, actor), to a fixed point. Use the same pattern as `parseDeviationDisclosure` in `scripts/lib/review-escalation.mjs` (~line 700), which defends against nested re-formation. Add a test showing that a reason with `<!-- reviewed-sha: <40 hex> --> <!-- cleared-human: x -->` (and a nested variant) produces a comment that `parseLatestHumanClearedSha` / `parseReviewedSha` do not count.

The other findings are follow-ups and do not block this PR: the dedupe key on identical recurring state, clear-claim liveness for wrapped workers, and the discarded-filter authorship scanner, which is already carded.

record.pattern: Operator-supplied text in a trusted comment must be ESCAPED (< to <, > to >), never stripped: delimiter-stripping regexes are incomplete sanitization (--!>, nested, partial forms survive).

rationale.body:
🔁 review — changes requested

Recorded by chalbert via claude-code-chat.

Operator decision (human review ceremony), 2026-10-13 ~17:45 ET, on head 6b8a973a7: **changes**. Operator: "Send back".

The forgery fix (6b8a973a7) strips HTML-comment delimiters from operator-supplied text. CodeQL reports 4 new high-severity alerts on it:
- `scripts/operations/operator-controls.mjs:24` and `scripts/operations/__tests__/operator-controls-regressions.test.mjs:19-20`: "Bad HTML filtering regexp" (only `-->` is recognized, not `--!>`), and "Incomplete multi-character sanitization" (a `<!--` can survive).

Required change: **escape instead of strip.** Render every operator-supplied string (reason, channel, actor) into the audit comment with `<` → `<` / `<` and `>` → `>` / `>`, the same way the JSON payload is already escaped. No HTML comment of any form (`-->`, `--!>`, nested, partial) can then appear in the rendered prose.

Keep the existing tests that a forged `reviewed-sha` / `cleared-human` reason is not counted by `parseLatestHumanClearedSha` / `parseReviewedSha`, and add `--!>` and partial/nested variants. The CodeQL check must come back clean.

record.pattern: Bulk backlog operations (close, reopen, consolidate) must preserve link integrity: never leave a closedInto pointer aimed at a closed survivor, and never produce a live card blockedBy a closed one.

rationale.body:
🔁 review — changes requested

Recorded by chalbert via claude-code-chat.

Operator decision (human review ceremony), 2026-10-13 ~17:25 ET, on head 6c580afa1: **changes**. Operator: "Send back".

The post-accept red team confirmed two broken edge cases on this head. Both corrupt backlog links, and this tool is about to close about 580 cards in bulk, so both must be fixed before approval.

1. **`scripts/operations/close-items.mjs:70`: closing a duplicate's survivor invalidates the `closedInto` pointers already aimed at it.** Fix: refuse to close a card while any closed duplicate points to it via `closedInto`, or re-point those duplicates to the new survivor (following the chain, with cycle protection). Record what moved, and make the dry run show it. Test: close A after B and C were closed into A.
2. **`scripts/operations/reopen-items.mjs:13`: reopening a dependent alone creates a forbidden live dependency on a closed blocker.** Fix: before reopening, check the card's `blockedBy`. Either refuse with a clear message naming the closed blockers, or reopen them too behind an explicit flag. Never produce a live card blocked by a closed one. Test: reopen D where D is blockedBy closed E.

Also, separate from this PR: the red-team gate did not send these confirmed breaks back on its own. That gap is being carded.

record.pattern: A mirror of our review verdict (e.g. native GitHub reviews) must reflect the LATEST state: dedupe on the latest matching record, not any earlier one, and dismiss the standing mirror when our verdict returns to pending.

rationale.body:
🔁 review — changes requested

Recorded by chalbert via claude-code-chat.

Operator decision (human review ceremony), 2026-10-13 ~17:35 ET, on head d12129b5b: **changes**. Operator: "Send back".

Mirror mode exists to measure agreement between our label verdicts and GitHub's native review state, over 50 verdicts. These findings make that measurement untrustworthy, and #4 must be fixed before any authoritative use.

1. **Dedupe on the bot's LATEST review, not any earlier match** (`scripts/lib/native-github-review.mjs:184-206`). With accepted → changes → accepted on one head, today it reports already-posted while GitHub shows the opposite, and logs agree=yes. Test: that exact flip-flop.
2. **When our verdict returns to pending (rearm/restamp), dismiss the bot's standing native review**, whether APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES (`:124`, `:148`). A pending label must never sit beside a standing bot APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES.
3. **The stale-review dismissal must work when the clearing verdict runs under a non-reviewer token,** e.g. the operator's clear-human (`:270`). Mint the reviewer role token for the dismissal, or queue it for the next reviewer-token run. Never leave the bot's CHANGES_REQUESTED standing after a clearance.
4. **Security: exact reviewer-bot identity** (`:178`). Login normalization must not let a human account match the configured reviewer bot. Compare the exact bot login, with the App's `[bot]` suffix and type, against the reviewer role's botLogin. Test: a human login that normalizes to the same string is refused.
5. Add a test pinning the `mirrorNativeReview` hook in `scripts/review-set-label.mjs:1876`: called after the label swap, with `to`, `headSha` and the pre-swap labels.

record.pattern: Never commit a local absolute path (home directory, host-specific key or file path); reference the resource by name and resolve it on the host.

rationale.operatorWords: "no local path should be committed ever"
rationale.body: Closed by the orchestrator: committed a host-local key path into scripts/settings/delivery-identity.json. Operator 2026-10-13 ~12:00 ET: "no local path should be committed ever". It is being redone with the key referenced by name and resolved on the host (no path in the repo), plus a gate that refuses committed home paths.

record.pattern: A finding or guard demanding that a childless epic carry a size is not real: sub-epic slices are deliberately scaffolded with no size because an epic is decomposed, never built directly.

rationale.operatorWords: "ok" to re-scoping: drop the epic-size guard entirely and keep only the workItem guard
rationale.body:
## Operator ruling (2026-10-13 ~13:40 ET): re-scoped to the retired-field guard only

The prepare was blocked as a spec-defect. The operator said "ok" to re-scoping: **drop the epic-size guard entirely and keep only the `workItem` guard.**

- The "sliced epic has no size" half is already enforced by the standards gate.
- The "childless epic must have a size" half reverses the slicing rule. A sub-epic slice is deliberately scaffolded with no size, because an epic is decomposed, never built directly (we:skills-src/split-backlog-item/SKILL.md, "Sub-epic slice").
- Every epic-size item in Design, Test plan and Done when below is therefore out of scope. Only the `workItem` parts remain.

record.pattern: When a finding names a policy choice, deliver it as a documented cascade setting with a protected default and a logged source layer; keep existing supported paths (e.g. lane clones) working rather than forbidding them.

rationale.operatorWords: "ok. using settings and policies if makes sense"
rationale.body:
## Operator ruling (2026-10-13 ~13:25 ET) — finding 2

The prepare was blocked with needs-ruling on finding 2: whether to reject ordinary clones by requiring linked worktrees, or keep clone support with a narrower Git-metadata permission. The operator chose (b), "ok. using settings and policies if makes sense":

- **Keep scratch clones and lane clones supported.** Every lane is an ordinary clone today, so requiring worktrees would break all Codex tasks.
- **Narrow what the sandbox may write.** Codex keeps write access to the git objects and refs it needs to commit, but `.git/hooks/` and `.git/config` are not writable inside the sandbox. Every git invocation in the sandboxed run carries `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.
- **As a setting/policy.** The protected git-metadata paths and the hooks override are a cascade setting (e.g. `codex.sandbox.gitMetadata { protectedPaths: ["hooks", "config"], disableHooks: true }`). It is documented and logs its source layer. The default is protected, and no layer may widen it without the override being logged.
- **Test.** A hook or config written by the sandboxed run is refused or never executed by a later git call. Also cover a linked-worktree gitdir and a clone gitdir.
- **Later option, not in this card.** Moving lanes to linked worktrees and then requiring them.

Findings 1, 3, 4 and 5 need no ruling and are delivered as written. Prefer a setting wherever a finding names a policy choice, e.g. the env allowlist in finding 3.
